doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Closing playback, singing, baritone and strings album
summary: He has taken up singing and baritone, and recalls a 1985 flute album with strings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well I just have to listen to this one more time before I go.
Let’s see if I can get this up here, because that is a nice way to wrap up.
Oh that’s pretty thanks. I still like to listen to these songs.
I have some things that I didn’t tell you about.
Oh, as I say I’m doing more scat singing now and also regular singing.
Oh yeah? Like what do you like to sing?

Oh well I like to sing, as I say my girlfriend would usually tell me I sound better when I sing up tunes, like happy tunes. Like I do “Lady Be Good” “Avalon” what are some of the other ones I do? Up tunes that I can scat on. “Indiana.” I like to sing all the pretty

ballads like, oh the past few days, “My Funny Valentine” about four times. Once as a bossa nova or a ballad, so I like to sing the lyrics, it’s nice. I may not be a Frank Sinatra or whatever it is, but it seems like I get some good response singing and also instrumentally, I’m getting some good response, and also I’m playing baritone lately, and that’s why I brought some of the things. There’s a few people here that you probably didn’t interview, playing with Carl Saunders, a friend of mine. He is getting a few more albums out. He has like a benefactor that’s putting in thousands, a doctor, that’s nice it’s always going to help.
Oh yeah. Love those doctors, don’t you?

I had someone in 1985 that put out, I think it’s listed here, that was kind of — Fernando Gelbart. He had some money and he says, I recorded with Frank Colette and he put the London Philharmonic Strings behind it. I didn’t bring the album, so twenty strings behind me and Frank Colette, most all flute. But as I say he had some money, so let’s do this. So I had four arrangers, George Calendrelli and some other people. But I haven’t recorded since then, that was I think in 1985. I forgot where I’m wandering to. But so as I say Carl was saying, “Oh you sound so great on baritone, you ought to just don’t play the other horns so much, just play baritone and flute. So occasionally I’ll bring the baritone, just to have another voice.
Yeah, you’ve got to think in a whole new key now too, right?
Well I was playing alto so that’s the alto key. So the alto, the tenor, the baritone, the piano, the flute the singing the scat — so that’s my act lately.
